headline: Shoprite to Eliminate Christo Wiese High-Voting Shares in R600M Deal
summary: South African retailer Shoprite has agreed to buy out and collapse the high-voting deferred share structure held by former chairman Christo Wiese in a transaction valued at R600 million.
why: Dual-class voting structures at major retail conglomerates have faced institutional investor resistance; unwinding them standardizes shareholder governance and voting parity.

impacts.name: Shoprite Holdings
impacts.why: Simplifying the capital structure eliminates voting distortion and improves corporate governance transparency.
